children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the equation of the tangent to $y=1-e^{-x}$ at the origin is $y=x$.

answer.short: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=e^{-x}$, so the gradient at the origin is $1$. Hence the tangent is $y=x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Deduce the equation of the normal at the origin without further use of calculus.

answer.worked:
The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so its gradient is $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}y-0&=-1(x-0)\\y&=-x\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the equation of the asymptote of this curve?

answer.worked: As $x\to\infty$, $e^{-x}\to0$, so $y\to1$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=1$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Sketch the curve, showing the points $T$ and $N$ where the tangent and normal respectively cut the asymptote.

answer.worked:
At $T$, the tangent $y=x$ meets $y=1$:
$$\begin{align*}x&=1\\T&=(1,1)\end{align*}$$
At $N$, the normal $y=-x$ meets $y=1$:
$$\begin{align*}-x&=1\\x&=-1\\N&=(-1,1)\end{align*}$$
The curve passes through the origin and approaches $y=1$ from below as $x$ increases.

spec.mathematics: Curve y=1-exp(-x); tangent y=x; normal y=-x; asymptote y=1; T=(1,1), N=(-1,1).

answer.worked:
$TN=1-(-1)=2$ and the perpendicular height from the origin to $TN$ is $1$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle OTN&=\frac12\times2\times1\\&=1\text{ square unit}\end{align*}$$
